title: Chain hoist
prompt: A labelled scale teaching model of the page 56 differential chain hoist hangs from an external gantry. Pull chain rotates the rigidly joined unequal upper chain wheels so the larger takes in more chain than the smaller lets out, lifting the lower load wheel and weight by the net difference. Reverse moves the same endless chain the other way and lowers the load. Let go removes the hand input and leaves this pictured hoist at rest. See-through shows both unequal upper wheels on their common axle, lower load wheel, chain engagement, continuous loop and hooks. Do not substitute a worm drive or add an unsourced brake.
blurb: A scale teaching adaptation of a differential chain hoist shows how unequal chain take-up lifts a load.
truthNotes: One endless chain passes over two unequal upper chain wheels fixed to a common axle and around the lower load wheel.
The external gantry and weight are teaching props. Dimensions, colours, separated wheel planes and slowed motion are illustrative.
The free hand loop sags as the load loop shortens. The lower wheel aligns with the two load strands.
Let go holds this pictured mechanism at rest. No brake or worm drive is represented and this is not a universal pulley claim.
Travel limits preserve the teaching model clearances.
Overlays and fixtures do not pad the anatomy count.

telemetry.reason: Standalone static figure has no production telemetry. Live verification untested.
